div.head: IV As 6.2
div.ab: Si episcopum uel comitem uel abbatem uel aldermannum uel thainum requirat, habeat terminum tres noctes. Et querat quicquid querat, non habeat uitam diucius, si capiatur.
Si episcopum vel comitem vel abbatem vel aldermannum vel thainum requirat, habeat terminum tres noctes; et quærat quicquid quærat, non habeat vitam diucius, si capiatur.
And if he seeks a bishop or a nobleman, an abbot an ealdorman or a thegn, he shall have a respite for three days. But let him seek whatever he may, he shall not be spared longer, if he is caught.
div.note: Latin only; no German translation in Liebermann. ‘uel comitem’ is probably originally a gloss on ‘aldermannum’ (Liebermann). Liebermann numbers the second sentence 6.2c. Old English in H (rows 849–851).
